_metadata.rubric: x04 rubric (natural-click standard + five content questions), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: Apart from the instructions file, I read only x04-pd-review-input.json and opened no other file, repository search, web page or paid API.

hints.reason: ASTRONAUT via going into orbit, GUM via the well-known Orbit gum brand; a space idea and a candy-aisle brand together make a clean two-sense click.

pairs.pair_note: A good brand double meaning; the astronaut side makes it feel like a real 'oh' moment.

hints.reason: BAND via the horn (brass) section, CAR via honking the horn; both senses are everyday.

pairs.pair_note: Solid and easy. On boards holding several horn words (DEVIL, UNICORN, FOG, SHOE) HORN becomes ambiguous.

hints.reason: BAND via the horn section, DEVIL via the devil's horns; the rock-concert 'devil horns' hand sign adds a bonus link.

pairs.pair_note: Fine as written; the explanation could also mention the rock 'devil horns' gesture, but it doesn't have to.

hints.reason: BAND via the horn section, UNICORN via its single horn; a pleasant contrast between a musical sense and an animal sense.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean double meaning.

hints.reason: BREAD via bread crust, EARTH via the geological crust from school science; a kitchen sense against a planet sense makes a satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: A classic school-science double meaning; one of the stronger CRUST pairs.

hints.reason: BREAD and PIE both via the baked crust (the same sense on both sides); instant but flat.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair. It uses the same sense twice, so there's little delight; DOUGH would be an equal alternative, not a better one.

hints.reason: BREAD and PIZZA both via the baked crust (the same sense); instant, low surprise.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy; DOUGH is an equally good alternative.

hints.reason: BREAD via its crust, RICH via the idiom 'upper crust'; the bread-is-money slang adds an extra layer.

pairs.pair_note: A nice idiom twist. DOUGH (bread dough, and dough as money) would also work well; both can pass.

hints.reason: CANDY via breath mints, CARD via 'mint condition' collectible cards; both senses are widely known.

pairs.pair_note: A good double meaning; 'mint condition' is familiar well beyond collectors.

hints.reason: CANDY via mints, CURRENCY via the U.S. Mint that makes coins; two completely different senses that click once seen.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best MINT pairs. The text correctly says coins (bills are printed elsewhere).

hints.reason: CANDY via mints is instant, but GARDEN via mint the plant is weak: MINT suggests an herb, not a garden, so players are unlikely to reach GARDEN on their own.

pairs.pair_note: The garden side is the weak link. A Wonka candy-garden angle exists but isn't clearly better; HERBS is a much better partner for MINT than GARDEN is.

hints.reason: CANDY via mints, GREEN via the color mint green (mint candies are often green too).

pairs.pair_note: Easy and clean.

hints.reason: CANDY via mints, HERBS via mint the herb; both instant, though the two senses are close (the candy is flavored with the herb).

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward; it works.

hints.reason: CAR via the car horn, DEVIL via the devil's horns; a pleasant contrast between a sound and a body part.

pairs.pair_note: Easy double meaning.

hints.reason: CAR via the car horn, FOG via the compound 'foghorn' (both are warning horns); both are instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join that earns its place: foghorn is very familiar, and both are warning-sound horns.

hints.reason: CAR via car keys, MAP via the map key (legend) taught in school; two distinct senses.

pairs.pair_note: Fine. A road-trip scene hint would also work, but KEY is the cleaner double meaning.

hints.reason: CAR via the ignition key, PIANO via its 88 keys; both are instant.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, easy double meaning.

hints.reason: CAR via car keys, PIE via 'key lime pie'; the phrase is instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Key lime pie is famous enough that the phrase-join clicks.

hints.reason: CAR via the car horn, SHOE via the shoehorn; the word is widely known even by people who never use one, and the sound-versus-tool contrast is pleasant.

pairs.pair_note: A slightly less instant compound than foghorn, but still broadly known.

hints.reason: CAR via car keys, TEST via the answer key; both are familiar.

pairs.pair_note: DMV (the driving test) is an equally strong scene hint for this pair, but KEY passes on its own.

hints.reason: CAR via honking the horn, UNICORN via its single horn; a fun, silly pairing.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and pleasant.

hints.reason: CARD via mint condition, HERBS via mint the herb; two distinct, familiar senses.

pairs.pair_note: Works fine.

hints.reason: CURRENCY via the U.S. Mint, HERBS via mint the plant; two unrelated senses make a satisfying reveal.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch: neither side gives away the other.

hints.reason: DEVIL and UNICORN both via horns on the head (the same sense); the evil-versus-pure contrast makes it fun.

pairs.pair_note: The same sense twice, but the contrast between the two creatures carries it.

hints.reason: EARTH via orbiting the Sun, GUM via the Orbit brand; both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Good; ASTRONAUT is the slightly more vivid partner, but this is fine.

hints.reason: EARTH via orbiting the Sun is instant, but MINT needs a two-step chain (Orbit, then gum, then mint flavor), so few players would land on it.

pairs.pair_note: The chained route is the problem; GUM is the natural partner for ORBIT, not MINT. I see no obvious better one-word hint for EARTH + MINT.

hints.reason: EARTH via the geological crust, PIZZA via pizza crust; two round things with layers make a fun visual pairing.

pairs.pair_note: A nice planet-as-pizza image; one of the best CRUST pairs.

hints.reason: EARTH via the Earth's crust, RICH via 'upper crust'; neither side is food, which makes the reveal less obvious.

pairs.pair_note: Works, though the RICH side relies on the idiom; on a board with BREAD, PIE or PIZZA, CRUST could pull players toward food.

hints.reason: GREEN via the color mint green, HERBS via mint the herb; both are clear.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: GUM via the Orbit brand, MOON via orbiting Earth; both are instant.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: GUM via the Orbit brand, NASA via launching spacecraft into orbit; both are clear.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: GUM via the Orbit brand, PLANET via planets orbiting the Sun; both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: GUM via the Orbit brand, SPACE via satellites in orbit; both clear.

pairs.pair_note: Solid. SPACE is a broad target, which keeps it easy.

hints.reason: GUM via the Orbit brand is instant, but STATION reaches orbit only through 'space station'; STATION on its own suggests train, gas or radio first.

pairs.pair_note: The STATION side needs an unstated 'space'; I see no obvious better one-word hint.

hints.reason: MAP via the map key (legend), PIANO via piano keys; two distinct, familiar senses.

pairs.pair_note: Clean.

hints.reason: MAP via the map key, PIE via 'key lime pie'; both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; the pie phrase is famous enough.

hints.reason: MAP via the map key, TEST via the answer key; both are reference-guide senses from school, so it's easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: The two senses are close cousins, but both are instantly recognizable.

hints.reason: PIANO via its keys, PIE via 'key lime pie'; the unlikely pairing of instrument and dessert gives a nice reveal.

pairs.pair_note: The most fun of the KEY pairs.

hints.reason: PIE and PIZZA both via the crust (the same sense); instant.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair. SLICE is an equally good alternative; neither is clearly better.

hints.reason: PIE via pie crust is instant, but players tie a geological crust to EARTH specifically, not to PLANET in general, so the planet side takes effort (the line is accurate).

pairs.pair_note: The same idea works much better as EARTH + PIE or EARTH + PIZZA; with PLANET the click is softer.
